concerns.message: Acceptance 6 (mooring at any speed) contradicts existing tests, but the task never names them as broken, and the constraint says to keep every existing test except those it names. The affected tests: simulation.test.ts:456 (the too-fast case doesn't moor), :465 (same with ahead held), and the corner-approach sweep at :521-556. That sweep starts at dockMaxSpeed and asserts `course[moored - 1].speed === 0` inside the dock tile, which fails once a ship moors on its first in-reach step at speed. Also web.test.ts:182 (the 'Slow down to dock' hint).
concerns.consequence: The worker either reports `question` and pauses the run, or rewrites and deletes these tests on its own. The coverage reviewer, which blocked the last run over test strength, may then flag the removed assertions. Treat them as named broken and say what replaces each one (for example, the corner test asserts a moor on the first in-reach step with a clear path).

concerns.message: Once the speed gate goes, `dockMaxSpeed` has no reader: only step.ts:52 and hud.ts:40 read it. Yet decisions.md's assumptions say the existing docking rules stay, `dockMaxSpeed` among them, and acceptance 2 keeps it in the literal baseline. sailing.ts:26-27 documents it as 'and its speed is at most this', and simulation.test.ts:341-342 still checks its ratio to full speed.
concerns.consequence: The run ships a dead tuning field. Its doc comment, and possibly docs/architecture.md, would describe a speed rule that no longer exists, and a test would guard the value of a number nothing reads. Decide now whether to keep it only as baseline data with a corrected comment, or remove it.

concerns.message: `HeadlessClient.hold` and `holdUntil` always send a neutral release when they finish (headlessClient.ts:177 and :190). If the stall integration test docks with `holdUntil(ahead+E, moored)`, that release resets `mooredThrottle` to 0 before the stall. Resuming with ahead held then casts off correctly, even with the fix in place. Also, if the test asserts 'still moored' right after resuming, it can pass before the server has run a world step on the resumed input.
concerns.consequence: The test fails for a reason unrelated to the lapse, and the worker may chase the wrong bug. Or the test passes without proving anything. The test should dock with raw `sendInput` calls (no release), and after resuming wait for the server frame to advance by at least two world steps before asserting the ship is moored.

concerns.message: The acceptance 6 sweep crosses every 8-unit heading 'into the berth's open sides' with lateral offsets across the reach, and requires the ship 'never ends up aground outside the reach'. That product includes cases where the correct rule still fails. Example: a ship offset to one side, heading away from the berth, or one whose straight path clips the land corner (like the diagonal case at simulation.test.ts:477-485). It doesn't moor, grounds against land beside the dock, slides along the coast out of the reach, and can ground there.
concerns.consequence: The worker adds ad-hoc exclusions, weakens the test, or reports `question`. Define the sweep geometrically: start just outside the reach, with headings within ±16 units of the bearing to the berth centre.

concerns.message: The sketch split crosses tooling boundaries. The entry script runs under plain `node` with type stripping, so it must import the generator as `./x.ts`. maps.test.ts is type-checked by packages/content/tsconfig.json: nodenext, no `allowImportingTsExtensions`, strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `types: []`. So it must import the generator with a `.js` specifier. The generator, written for loose Node stripping, also joins content's strict typecheck for the first time.
concerns.consequence: `npm run typecheck` fails with TS5097 or strictness errors, or `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` breaks. The worker loses a check cycle on it. State the import convention: test imports `.js`, entry imports `.ts`.

concerns.message: The suggested route for acceptance 7 changes what a missing `StepInputs` entry means: from 'neutral' to 'neutral, but keep a moored ship's latch'. The encounters feature, running at the same time in packages/simulation/src/encounters, may build or omit `StepInputs` entries (for example, for reserved ships) on the old assumption that missing means neutral.
concerns.consequence: After merge, a ship without an entry keeps a stale moored latch, or encounter tests that call `step(..., {})` behave differently, and nobody notices because the two runs never see each other's code.

simpler_alternative: For acceptance 7, fix it in the server only and leave the simulation's input contract alone. In `MatchRoom.advance`, when a player's gate has lapsed and their ship is moored, pass `{ buttons: 0, moveX: 0, moveY: -ship.mooredThrottle }` instead of neutral. In the moored branch of `sail` (step.ts:47), that input counts as 'the throttle it moored with is still held', so it returns the ship unchanged: it doesn't move and the latch stays. step.ts, the `StepInputs` doc and the parallel encounters feature's assumption that a missing entry is neutral all stay as they are. The stall integration test still proves the fix.
cheap_experiment: In a scratch worktree, delete `&& Math.abs(ship.speed) <= tuning.dockMaxSpeed` from step.ts:52 and run the simulation and web unit tests. That shows exactly which existing tests the new rule breaks (expected: :456, :465, the :521-556 corner sweep and web.test.ts:182), so the task can name them before a worker starts. In the same run, add a throwaway loop over the proposed sweep (8-unit headings × lateral offsets × speeds 0, 19 and 39, at the corner dock) that logs any case that grounds outside the reach. That shows whether the 'never aground outside the reach' clause can be met as written or needs a tighter heading window. It takes about ten minutes.
